Big Tech really wants to put a computer on your face.

Google Glass tried it. Snapchat keeps trying it. Meta is now making an alarming number of smart glasses, despite the minor issue that most people have spent the last decade not asking for them.

And to be fair, some of the new ones are actually useful. They can translate things, identify objects and take photos without pulling out your phone. They can also put a camera directly on your face, which creates several fun new ways to secretly film strangers.

Let's look at why companies like Meta, Google and Snapchat are so determined to make smart glasses happen, what they actually get out of having cameras pointed wherever we're looking, and whether AI glasses are finally here to stay.
